title: Three Seasons and One Short Brush
subtitle: 艺术殿堂 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 艺术殿堂（文学艺术与体育·绘画、建筑等领域的代表作品和人物）
meta: 主题语境：艺术殿堂（文学艺术与体育·绘画、建筑等领域的代表作品和人物）　|　核心词汇：poster　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 poster 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1965 the painter ① designed the poster that no visitor in the studio would have noted, and he said the designing was the whole of the season. The ② poster, meaning the notice itself and not the brush, ran three seasons and stayed unnoted in the book; a poster, he said, is the only thing in a studio that is judged by how long it is left unnoted.

Every ③ poster in that studio had the same short brush beside it, and the ④ poster at the far easel, meaning the sketch they kept for the children to keep and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A poster, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to note; the painter said the noting is the part that fills three seasons.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the poster was the whole of the matter, meaning the appeal and not the notice. The ⑥ poster, meaning the appeal and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody notes; poster, he said, is either something you design or the only word that means both a notice and an appeal. He said the appeal is the part they remember.

By 1970 the ⑦ poster had become a line in a catalogue, and the catalogue had become an argument about the short brush. The ⑧ poster of the whole thing, the painter wrote in May, was one studio and three seasons of noting; poster, he said, is either the sketch at the far easel or the reason you learned to note. He said the noting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ poster I remember is the notice noted in the catalogue, which closed in 1972 and is still noted as the quietest in the studio. A ⑩ poster, my mother said in 1974, is the only notice that improves by being noted; every poster, she said, is an appeal that has agreed to look like a notice. She said the appeal was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 海报；招贴（指画室里每一张旁边的那一张）
B. n. 海报；招贴（指那张海报本身，与小小的画笔相对）
C. 固定搭配：design the poster 设计这一张海报
D. n. 海报；招贴（指留给孩子们留着的那一幅）
E. n. 海报之事（抽象总称，指一处画室的海报之事）
F. n. 海报；招贴（指展品目录里写到、被记下的那一张）
G. n. 海报、号召（指一件事里人人都看却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 号召（抽象总称，指人人都看却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: designed the poster that no visitor in the studio would have noted
The poster, meaning the notice itself and not the brush
the poster at the far easel
the poster was the whole of the matter
the poster had become a line in a catalogue
The poster of the whole thing
A poster, my mother said in 1974

answers.why: design the poster 意为“设计这一张海报”，1965 年那位画师把画室里没有一位观者肯记下的一张海报做了一遍。
poster 意为“海报；招贴”，指那张海报本身而不是小小的画笔，它经过了三个季度而在簿子上没有被记下。
poster 意为“海报；招贴”，指画室里每一张旁边的那一张，每一张旁边都有同一支小小的画笔。
poster 意为“海报；招贴”，指最远那副画架的留给孩子们留着的那一幅，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
poster 意为“海报、号召”，指一件事里人人都看却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这张号召就是那件事的全部。
poster 意为“号召”，指人人都看却无人提起的那样东西而不是那张海报，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
poster 意为“海报；招贴”，指展品目录里写到、被记下的那一张，到 1970 年这一张成了展品目录里的一行。
poster 意为“海报之事”，画师五月写道，整件事的海报之事是一处画室和三个季度的记下。
poster 意为“海报；招贴”，我记得的是展品目录里记下过的那一张，1972 年画成了，至今仍被说成画室里最安静的一张。
poster 为抽象总称，母亲 1974 年说，海报是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的海报。
